title: Streamline fluid spacing units and depth layers for responsive data surfaces
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Modernize the design token set for spacing, radius, and elevation to a fluid system that scales across breakpoints and reduces token churn for data-heavy surfaces (tables, charts, dense cards). This ticket formalizes the token names, argues for semantic depth layers, and proposes a migration plan + tooling to update components and run visual regressions.

Motivation: Current token set has grown organically: static step tokens (spacing-1..12), multiple radius variants per component, and several ad-hoc shadow presets. This is causing inconsistent spacing in dense views, unexpected layout shifts on responsive breakpoints, and duplicate maintenance down the component tree. A fluid base (4px->rem clamp) plus a semantic depth layer model reduces the number of tokens consumers use and centers behavior around intent (surface/elevated/overlay).

Design decisions: 
- Base unit: move to a 4px grid as canonical design unit, expose fluid spacing tokens using CSS clamp() mapped to rems for cross-device consistency. Example token: spacing-fluid-1 -> clamp(0.25rem, 0.8vw, 0.5rem).
- Semantic aliases: introduce spacing-inline-small/medium/large and spacing-stack-small/medium/large that map to fluid units. Encourage use of semantic aliases in components instead of numeric steps.
- Radius: consolidate corner tokens into radius-container, radius-control, radius-chip with responsive overrides for compact mode. Reduce per-component custom radii.
- Depth layers: replace ad-hoc shadow names with depth.surface, depth.elevated.1..3, depth.overlay. Each depth token is a single semantic alias that expands to a shadow token set (offset, blur, spread, alpha) so runtime systems can pick optimized kernels and devs can reason about intent rather than values.
- Shadow recipe: adopt two-layer shadow recipe (soft ambient + directional key) with variables for alpha and y-offset. Provide WebGL-friendly numeric fallbacks for canvas renderers used in charts.
- Accessibility checks: ensure contrast of content against surface and elevated surfaces remains >= WCAG AA for body text. Run automated contrast tests across the token palette and report any regressions.

Trade-offs & constraints: 
- Fluid spacing improves responsiveness but slightly complicates precision for pixel-perfect mocks; we'll provide static token aliases for design handoff.
- Consolidation reduces freedom for component owners; we'll keep escape hatch tokens for exceptional cases but discourage their use.
- Changing shadow semantics may affect perceived elevation; visual regression suite is mandatory before rollout.

Outcomes: 
1) Single source of truth for spacing/radius/elevation with semantic aliases used across components.
2) Migration codemod for the UI repo that replaces numeric spacing tokens with semantic aliases where appropriate.
3) Updated design kit and component docs + Figma tokens.

acceptance_criteria: Design tokens for spacing, radius, and depth published to tokens package with semantic aliases
Components (button, table, chart card) updated to use semantic aliases in code and docs
Codemod PR submitted and passes CI with automated visual diffs showing no critical regressions
Contrast tests across surface/elevated combos show no WCAG AA regressions for body text
Migration guide + design handoff created and linked from the tokens spec
Deprecated raw numeric tokens are flagged in tokens package with clear timeline and warnings
implementation_notes: Add token JSON + CSS variables to packages/tokens (tokens/v3/fluid.json)
Write codemod that maps spacing-(\n) to spacing-inline-{small|medium|large} based on heuristics (table dense -> stack-small)
Expose runtime aliasing for depth tokens so serving layer can substitute optimized shadows for canvas rendering
Add visual-diff job that runs changed components (buttons, tables, charts) at three breakpoints and compares against baseline
Coordinate with ENG-4021 for build changes to tokens package and with ENG-5178 for chart runtime shadow fallbacks

2026-03-05 Marco P (Eng): Confirmed chart runtime can accept depth tokens as numeric shadow recipes; will add fallback API in ENG-5178.
2026-03-07 Design review: Need to provide static snapshot tokens for design handoff; Figma plugin might need a small change to export clamp() values as tokens.
